fixes.explanation: Good guess, friend, because those names do show up in Numbers. Joshua and Caleb are two of the men who explored the land, and they urged Israel not to be afraid (Numbers 14:6, 9). But in this passage, the finders bring the man to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation (Numbers 15:33). No elders are named here. Joshua and Caleb are good names, but they aren't on the guest list for this one.

Edom, friend! Esau's family tree goes there, and Genesis 36:1 says so outright: "Esau (that is, Edom)." Good name to know, but it's the wrong address on this envelope. God says He is the LORD their God "…who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Numbers 15:41) Egypt is the land He names, and He says it right out loud.

problems.problem: The passage does not say the whole camp is about to find out what happened. It says the man was brought to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation.
The statement that Edom appears elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference, since it is a fact from outside this passage.
The explanation is flat and generic. It repeats that Egypt is the land named without much of Papa Dorin's voice.
